description: The page a subscriber reaches from the campaign email: the merge tag supplies a first name and the band greets them with it — 'Ben, let's go further together.' — in gold above the headline. Read the frame against its 'Public Visitor' pair, which is pixel-identical to this one everywhere except that line, because THAT asymmetry is the design decision. The recomposition made the network the page's hero and dropped the photo hero that used to personalize by swapping its whole headline; this band cannot do that, since 'A grid, lit from within' is the picture's own caption and trading it away would delete the composition the band exists to be. So the greeting is ADDITIVE: a named arrival gets a line nobody else sees, and the public visitor gets the page the team signed off on, untouched. It is filled in the BROWSER — the site is a static build, so the name does not exist when the HTML is written — which is also why a hostile `?name=` is rejected rather than rendered (`applyNetworkGreeting` in momentumNetworkDom.ts, asserted in its unit tests). The testimonials seed here is now incidental: the impact band sits far below a viewport capture, and 'The Impact Band With Real Quotes' reorders it into frame to prove that state properly.
